title: Real KaTeX glyph compositor experiment
summary: Superseded before implementation because the initial contract omitted required typed autonomy fields; no slice work began.

sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.
Human-approved 24-slice proposal, preservation boundary, complexity budget, visual checkpoint, and stop conditions.

allowedWork: Slices 1-12 may build one isolated real-KaTeX solve-x compositor exemplar using the existing material layer, computed-style clone, font readiness, semantic motion selectors, lineage matcher, and bounded scheduler.
Slices 13-24 remain gated until explicit human promotion after slice 12, then may generalize the same compositor to fraction merge, plus-minus split, and one crowded responsive case.
Add at most four focused compositor production modules and six generic lifecycle primitives; commit and verify each slice independently.
disallowedWork: Stop if semantic selectors require undocumented KaTeX-tree guessing, if solve-x still reads as crossfade or character substitution, or if one shared correction cannot eliminate native handoff jump.
No operation-, fraction-, quadratic-, branch-, or viewport-specific scheduler; no durable DOM, glyph geometry, keyframes, or backend plans; clones never own accessibility or interaction.
No radical repair, family rollout, Manim implementation, Python runtime, video encoding, CAS, live LLM API, new renderer family, curriculum expansion, or unrelated user work.
goal: Determine whether actual rendered KaTeX fragments can produce convincing object-constant solve-x motion and, only after human promotion, generalize through one semantic-constrained compositor.
